capability_notes.floating_point_classification: Type-preserving single-evaluation C macros and libc++ overloads classify binary32/binary64/binary128 values. Shared binary128 comparison helpers inspect both words, including NaNs and signed zero; other quad arithmetic/conversion helpers still narrow through double and do not provide general binary128 precision. Existing unsupported math functions remain unavailable.
capability_notes.integer_conversion: C-locale strtol/strtoul and wcstol/wcstoul (32-bit long), strtoll/strtoull/strtoimax/strtoumax and their wide counterparts (64-bit). One checked parser reads full byte/wchar elements without transcoding or narrowing wide input. ASCII whitespace/digits, bases 2..36 and octal/hex auto-detection; no binary prefix or Unicode classification. Invalid bases return EINVAL; overflow saturates with ERANGE while consuming all digits. No conversion leaves endptr at the original input; other successful conversions preserve errno. Wide endptr offsets count wchar_t elements.
capability_notes.floating_point_environment: Fixed Wasm round-to-nearest arithmetic, FE_ALL_EXCEPT=0 and no host floating-point state. Empty exception/default-environment operations succeed; unsupported modes, flags and malformed saved environments fail. No dynamic rounding or sticky exception support.
capability_notes.resources: Public time64 timeval-based rusage. Guest CPU accounting is unavailable: getrusage returns -1/ENOSYS for SELF/CHILDREN, -1/EINVAL otherwise, without accessing output. Resource-limit storage is the existing libc compatibility facade; kernel enforcement is not claimed.
capability_notes.default: Existing partial WASTE application ABI; availability and Wasm signatures do not imply full C/POSIX conformance.
capability_notes.locale: Fixed C.UTF-8 facade; setlocale ignores the requested locale/category, uselocale is a compatibility stub. No locale object lifecycle API.
capability_notes.wide_characters: Signed 32-bit wchar_t memory comparison/copy/move/fill and NUL-terminated length/comparison/search, including reverse, set and substring searches. Memory counts are wide elements and searches/compares preserve embedded NUL handling. Existing limited classification/UTF-8 conversion subset remains; no complete Unicode classification, stateful encoding or wide stream formatted IO claim.
capability_notes.stdio: Guest-owned opaque FILE; formatting/scanning implement the existing subset, not all standard conversions.
capability_notes.filesystem: Engine-owned in-memory namespace, retained hard-link inodes, symbolic links and descriptors; adapters enforce supported flags and errno. Link counts describe each cloned namespace, reconciled at reap; immediate cross-process namespace visibility and deletion reconciliation remain pending. No host filesystem access.
capability_notes.threads: Guest mutex helpers are single-threaded compatibility stubs; pthread creation, conditions, rwlocks and TLS APIs are unavailable.
capability_notes.network: Current syscall wrappers are unsupported without a capability provider; no raw socket or DNS capability is added by headers.
capability_notes.processes: Shared engine fork/exec/wait scheduling in both runtimes. execv uses the current guest environ and exact path; wait selects any child through waitpid(-1, ..., 0). waste_waitpid_until uses an absolute monotonic deadline, existing signal/restart state and readiness scheduling; expiry leaves the child alive. Invalid exec pointers and wait output buffers return EFAULT without replacement/reaping. Actual LLVM finite Wait/ExecuteAndWait use the same deadline API, preserving application alarms; polling expiry retains the child and ordinary expiry kills/reaps the exact target. posix_spawn, vfork, child CPU accounting, memory budgets and CPU affinity remain unavailable.
capability_notes.dynamic_loading: Existing engine-owned handles and installed Wasm DSO loader; no native host-library loading.
capability_notes.mapping: Existing engine mappings, i64 offsets and bounded permissions; MAP_FIXED unsupported. No claim of host mmap semantics.
capability_notes.ncurses: Configured pinned DSO, unsigned four-byte NCURSES_BOOL. Missing optional/debug/SP entry points are compile-time unavailable.
capability_notes.assert: Default assert uses compiler trap; no diagnostic text or SIGABRT delivery. NDEBUG omits evaluation.
capability_notes.abort: Guest libc calls waste_kernel.abort_v1. SIGABRT terminates the guest, including ignored/blocked signals and returning handlers; waitpid records signal 6. A caught handler runs synchronously and may not suspend. Host runtime and parent remain alive.
capability_notes.exit: Shared guest libc retains allocation-backed C atexit and C++ __cxa_atexit registrations, retires callbacks before invocation and finalizes in reverse order. __cxa_finalize(dso) selects matching entries; callbacks may use ordinary evaluator yields. Normal exit finalizes then requests fflush and immediate kernel termination. Successful exec discards registrations through the existing allocator bootstrap; rejected exec preserves them and fork clones private state. _Exit and signal termination bypass callbacks. Automatic C++ DSO finalization on dlclose, concurrent registration and buffered flush conformance are not established.
capability_notes.clocks: clock_gettime reads CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC through injected kernel callbacks. Invalid destinations return EFAULT, unsupported IDs EINVAL, absent callbacks ENOSYS. No CPU clocks, setters or POSIX timer suite are advertised. Public alarm uses one process-owned monotonic deadline through waste_kernel.alarm_v1 (i32 seconds, i64 remaining/error); expiry queues SIGALRM, fork clears the child timer and exec preserves it. Replacement/cancellation round remaining seconds up; cancellation retains pending signals.
capability_notes.signals: Engine-owned 128-bit signal sets and process dispositions; compiled ordinary C handlers use the shared function table, while table-free legacy WAT handlers retain their local-index ABI. Public sigaction uses the fixed 24-byte waste_kernel.sigaction_v1 boundary and returns -1/errno; signal installs a persistent SA_RESTART handler. Unsupported action flags return EINVAL without changing state or output. SIGKILL/SIGSTOP cannot be blocked or caught. Delivery uses existing self-signal, read, pselect, wait and bounded opcode boundaries; handlers may not suspend. siginfo callbacks, alternate stacks and machine fault contexts are unavailable. kill(pid, 0) queries allocated processes including zombies, with ESRCH after reap; all-process broadcast and full permission/job-control semantics remain outside this verified boundary.
capability_notes.floating_conversion: C-locale narrow/wide strtof/strtod/strtold and wcstof/wcstod/wcstold. Decimal/hex ASCII grammar, optional valid exponents, infinity and canonical quiet NaN; wide input retains complete wchar values. Bounded integer ratios round directly to binary32/64/128, nearest ties-to-even, without a double intermediate. Overflow returns signed infinity/ERANGE; inexact tiny results set ERANGE, exact subnormals preserve errno. No conversion returns positive zero with the original endptr. Successful conversion preserves errno. Accepted NaN payload spellings map to a canonical value; no Unicode classification, alternate locales or dynamic rounding support.
capability_notes.wide_formatting: Bounded swprintf/vswprintf count signed four-byte wchar elements. Integer flags/lengths, pointer/count conversions, full wide strings/characters and fixed UTF-8 strings; width/precision count output elements. f/F/e/E/g/G/a/A format exact binary64/128 encodings with integer decimal/hex digits and nearest ties-to-even, without double narrowing of long double. Success preserves errno; nonzero capacity receives a terminated prefix. Insufficient/zero capacity returns -1/EOVERFLOW, invalid format syntax returns EINVAL, invalid UTF-8 returns EILSEQ. No positional arguments, grouping, alternate locale or stateful encoding. Narrow printf floating output and wide stream IO remain unimplemented.
capability_notes.non_local_jumps: Engine-owned copyable evaluator checkpoints, with direct caller imports and exported mutable i32 __stack_pointer. setjmp/longjmp and sigsetjmp/siglongjmp normalize a zero jump value to one and reject inactive tokens. Nonzero sigsetjmp save_mask flags retain and restore the process kernel mask with the checkpoint; zero flags leave mask changes intact. No native machine context or Asyncify.
capability_notes.randomness: getrandom/getentropy use runtime cryptographic entropy (native OS or browser Web Crypto); unavailable entropy fails explicitly. GRND_NONBLOCK and GRND_RANDOM are accepted using the same secure source; unsupported flags are rejected. rand/arc4random retain the deterministic compatibility PRNG and must not seed keys.
